title: One-step gate transformation
statement: For $n\in\mathbb N$, a state $(G,t,N)$ consisting of a finite list $G$ of gates, a map $t\colon\mathbb N\to\mathbb N$, and a counter $N\in\mathbb N$, and a gate $g$ with argument list of length $k$, define the next state as follows. Append to $G$ a gate of the same kind as $g$ whose arguments are the images under $t$ of the arguments of $g$, then one negation gate reading each such image, then $k$ negation gates reading, in order, the vertices $n+|G|+1$ through $n+|G|+k$. The new map sends $N$ to $n+|G|$; for any other vertex appearing among the arguments of $g$, it sends that vertex to $n+|G|+1+k$ plus the index of its first occurrence in the argument list; on all remaining vertices it agrees with $t$. The counter increases to $N+1$.
hypotheses_covered: state consisting of a finite gate list, a map from natural numbers to natural numbers, and a natural-number counter
